event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_alab: Packed sand around the stakes keeps the remaining canvas down.
Bury the stakes
The group abandons the canvas and waits out the gust behind the axles.
Move behind the carts
The canvas tears free of your hands and a frame hits you before flying into the sand.
You use the wind to fold the whole structure cleanly without losing a single rope.
You hold one side, but two families lose their shade in the gust.
You pull the canvas flat and pin the corners before the next blast hits.
Pin the canvas
A sandstorm hits a caravan stop and tears loose the large shade canvas. Families crouch behind carts while the stakes pull out of the ground one by one.
Canvas in the Wind
The number matches the ledger; the clerk corrects the seal without seizing the cargo.
Compare the ledger
You pass the checkpoint while the two men continue arguing.
Leave the dispute
The goods stay cool while the merchant fixes the paperwork.
Shade the cargo
A clerk stops a cart at a checkpoint because its transport seal is stamped upside down. The merchant swears another office cleared it, but the sun is beginning to spoil the cargo.
The Reversed Seal
The family fills the canteen without reducing the shared reserve.
Give your ration
The keeper measures everyone equally and finds enough margin for the child.
Measure every canteen
The rule holds, but the family leaves with only its original ration.
Respect the queue
At a roadside stop, a cistern keeper refuses an extra canteen to a family whose child is coughing in the heat. Behind them, the line counts its own rations and starts protesting.
One Canteen Too Many
The keeper closes the channel and accepts a lost day to avoid permanent damage.
Close for repairs
You force the wrong gate and water spills into a secondary canal that is already full.
You also reset the worn stop, preventing the gate from jamming on the next cycle.
You free part of the mechanism, but the flow remains too weak to satisfy the line.
You spot the stone jammed under the rack and restore the main channel.
Inspect the rack
All three plots receive less water, but none is completely cut off.
Share the weak flow
An irrigation gate refuses to open while three farmers wait for their water turn. The keeper fears breaking the rack, and each farmer already blames the previous one for forcing it.
The Jammed Sluice
You choose a track that is too fresh and lead the cart into deeper sand.
You spot a nearly invisible gravel strip that saves the whole caravan hours.
You find a way through, but a wheel sinks and half the sacks must be unloaded.
You read the older ruts and guide the cart over the firmest ground.
Find firm ground
You plant markers toward a longer but passable loop.
Mark a detour
The sacks move by hand and the cart rises enough to roll again.
Unload the cart
A date cart sinks to its axle on a road erased by wind. The next caravan is approaching and cannot pass around it without entering soft dunes.
Axle in the Sand
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_cact: You turn the marker onto the wrong bearing; a fisher shouts before correcting your mistake.
You also find a second mark carved underneath for ships coming from Reverse Mountain.
The current hides the clue and you cannot prove which way the board should point.
Salt deposits and brush strokes reveal the marker's original direction.
Inspect the traces
You mark the rock so the next crew checks the board before trusting its bearing.
Add a warning
You reset the board as the fisher says and note the symbol painted on its back.
Trust the fisher
On a rocky point, a painted board marks the coastal current in the wrong direction. A fisher says someone turned it overnight, just before several ships arrived.
The Backward Marker
You misread the gauge and open an almost empty valve, drawing shouts from the whole line.
You find a hidden leak; fixing it restores enough water to calm both lines.
Your estimate convinces nobody and the argument keeps the cistern blocked.
You spot a secondary line that is still full and split the wait between two taps.
Read the gauge
Each line gets a reduced ration and the cistern lasts until evening.
Propose a split
Your group steps back; the tension falls, but you will need to find water elsewhere.
Yield your turn
At the harbor cistern, locals refuse to serve a crew that arrived before dawn. The gauge is falling fast, and two lines begin shoving around the same valve.
The Contested Cistern
You wedge a beam under the bollard and the dockhands slowly haul the skiff back.
Brace the mooring
The line lashes your face and the skiff hits the rocks before anyone regains it.
You recover the skiff and secure the neighboring moorings too.
You catch the line too late; several crates end up in the water.
You pin the skiff against the pier before the gust can take it again.
Grab the line
A few crates are sacrificed, but the skiff stops dragging the line.
Cut loose the crates
A gust tears loose a skiff loaded with fresh water. It drifts toward a cactus-covered shore while two dockhands cling to a rope burning through their hands.
Skiff in the Thorns
You clear scrub around the stores and the fire runs out of fuel.
Dig a firebreak
More hands arrive quickly enough to hold the fire line.
Ring the harbor bell
The watchmen move the jars while the fire burns only across the ridge.
Save the water stores
A signal fire jumps its stone ring and catches dry scrub. Watchmen haul buckets from the harbor, but the wind is already driving flames toward their stores.
Fire on the Ridge
The shed comes down before the flames reach it, creating a second fuel break.
Pull down the shed
The watchmen let the empty shed burn and keep the water for the fire line.
Save the water for the line
The soaked rope refuses to catch when sparks arrive.
Soak the rope
The firebreak is barely holding when the wind shifts and drives the flames toward a shed packed with dry rope. The watchmen have only one barrel of water within reach.
The Wind Turns
Vendors lend their brooms and the lane reopens before a child is hurt.
Sweep the spines
The porter admits the strap snapped; the sabotage accusation dies down.
Question the porter
You skirt the dispute and reach the pier without getting involved.
Take the back lane
A basket of cactus pulp bursts in the market lane. Spines roll under sandals, a vendor accuses a sailor of sabotage, and the crowd blocks the only path to the pier.
The Thorn Market
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_drum: You block the snow and give the staff enough calm to work.
Hold the door
The crew Medic takes over triage and assigns places without wasting time.
Let the Medic lead
You misclassify two symptoms and the clinic loses precious minutes correcting the order.
You reorganize the room so cleanly that the staff free a bed before the next sled arrives.
Your triage reduces the crush but does not solve the bed shortage.
You clearly separate cold emergencies from mechanical injuries and speed up treatment.
Triage the patients
A mountain clinic receives three patients almost at once: frostbite, a broken leg, and fever. Only one table is free, relatives all talk at once, and snow blows through the door.
The Full Clinic
You block access and send the line toward a longer but safer detour.
Close the bridge
The ice breaks under your step and you drop waist-deep into black water.
You find a line of old ice that even lets the baskets cross without overloading it.
You reach the middle, but villagers must abandon their baskets to retreat.
You stagger the crossings so no two heavy loads share the same ice plate.
Guide the crossings
The loads stay on the bank while the villagers cross lighter.
Unload the baskets
The frozen bridge between two hamlets cracks beneath a line of loaded villagers. The railing is locked in ice, and the river is already carrying away broken slabs.
The Ice Bridge
Everyone gets out before the awning collapses onto the tables.
Clear the stalls
Two emergency posts hold long enough to clear the snow.
Prop the beam
The cashbox is saved, but the vendors abandon the remaining goods under the awning.
Save the common cashbox
Accumulated snow bends the market awning over several stalls. Vendors grab their cash instead of leaving, and a beam starts splitting above them.
The Overloaded Awning
You brace too low; the snow sweeps you away with the sled for several meters.
You also clear a safe pocket where the carriers can wait out the slides.
You slow the sled, but a second wave of snow pins it beneath a ledge.
You take the slope at an angle and guide the sled out of the avalanche chute.
Brace the sled
The carriers abandon the heaviest crates and save the rest of the medicine.
Split the load
Villagers climb up with ropes before the slope moves again.
Signal the village
An avalanche cuts a trail above a village and shoves a medicine sled toward the edge. Two carriers hold the rope, but a new crack is already running across the slope behind them.
The Medicine Sled
One crate vanishes under snow, but the carriers keep the rest.
Abandon the outer crate
The medicine goes under a ledge before snow crosses the shelf.
Drag the crates under rock
Everyone shelters behind the sled until the slide passes.
Shield the carriers
Another rumble starts above the sled. The second slide is smaller, but it is aimed at the shelf where the carriers set the rescued crates.
The Second Slide
The crew Navigator cross-checks the terrain and brings you back onto the marked line.
Follow the Navigator
The strips remain visible at hand height even after snow covers the stakes.
Tie cloth markers
You lead the travelers back to harbor before visibility worsens.
Walk them back
A whiteout erases the red stakes marking the path from harbor to high ground. Travelers circle the same rock while their tracks disappear behind them.
Markers in the Whiteout
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_jaya: The crowd backs under awnings before the largest debris lands.
Clear the quay
Drivers pull their carts out of the area and clear the lane.
Move the carts
You note unusual shells and wear marks before salvagers take everything.
Study the debris
An upward current bursts offshore and rains pieces of wood, fish, and a cracked bell onto the harbor. Bystanders stare upward instead of leaving the falling zone.
Rain from Above
You trust the cleanest drawing, which happens to copy a false current legend.
You find a coastal detail absent from originals and identify the table where the copies were altered.
You prove the charts contradict each other without determining which was copied first.
The same scale errors appear across several sheets and reveal a single workshop.
Compare the scales
You keep only the useful annotations for comparison without trusting the drawn route.
Keep one as a clue
The crews pocket their money and the seller folds his table under boos.
Warn the buyers
A vendor sells charts supposedly showing rising currents toward the sky. Three crews compare their purchases and find islands drawn in different places on every copy.
Charts of the Sky
A plank gives way and you finish hanging from a halyard under the dock's laughter.
You touch the mark, climb down cleanly, and turn the wager back on the one who challenged you.
You reach the mast, but your rival touches the mark first.
You use the ship's roll to gain the last length of rope.
Climb for the pennant
You tell an impossible exploit; the crowd forgets the race to argue over your lie.
Answer with a story
The sailor finds another challenger and the crowd drifts back toward the tavern.
Refuse the bet
On the dock, a drunken sailor bets that no outsider can touch a pennant atop an old rig before he does. The crowd is already pushing both competitors toward the shrouds.
Rigging Wager
The auctioneer repeats the rules loudly enough to draw nearby dockworkers.
Demand a public bid
You leave the locals to settle their power struggle without involving your crew.
Leave the auction
The lumber moves into a locked warehouse before any buyer is forced to yield.
Move the lot inside
A salvage-lumber auction turns ugly when three men surround the auctioneer and announce the lot already belongs to them. Other buyers close their purses and look for the exit.
The Rough Auction
The weight drops away and the partners haul the diver up more easily.
Cut the salvage bag
The crew Medic sets the pace and brings the diver up without rushing him.
Let the Medic take over
You pull too early: the rope burns your palms and the diver strikes the edge on the way up.
You recover both diver and bag without letting the rope foul beneath the pier.
You bring him back conscious, but his salvage bag sinks with the cut line.
You pace the ascent and the diver catches his breath before reaching the dock.
Pace the ascent
A salvage diver surfaces too quickly beside the pier and clings to his line without answering. His partners hesitate between hauling him up immediately or keeping him in the water a moment longer.
The Pale Diver
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_litt: From a fallen trunk, you spot a longer loop back to camp.
Climb for a view
You mistake a fresh trail for a safe path and emerge in front of a predator that sends you running back.
You find a rise that also reveals the next dangerous area before you enter it.
You avoid the herd, but the detour keeps you away from camp for a long time.
The tracks reveal a recent opening that lets you cross between two animal passes.
Read the tracks
You let the herd pass and lose several hours, but no animal spots you.
Wait under cover
Trees shake ahead of camp, then a gigantic herd cuts across the only clear trail. Tracks overlap in the mud, and a closer roar announces something following the herbivores.
The Crushed Trail
The group follows its own tracks back before the parent appears.
Backtrack quietly
You let the massive shape pass between the trees without touching the nest.
Hide beneath the roots
A discreet marker will keep later travelers from taking this detour.
Mark the nest from afar
The detour opens onto a huge nest built between two roots. A cracked egg moves in the leaves while the roar heard earlier closes in behind the group.
At the Nest Edge
A drainage cut diverts the water before it reaches the sleeping area.
Cut a drain
Your shove sends the wrong trunk moving and a mass of ferns crashes onto you.
You turn the fall into a stable walkway above the soaked undergrowth.
You clear a narrow gap, but camp remains cut off from its water source.
You identify the load-bearing trunk and open a corridor without bringing the rest down.
Find the load-bearing trunk
The camp retreats to drier ground and gives up the path for the day.
Move the tents
After a downpour, giant ferns and trunks collapse across the camp path. Water pools behind the vegetal dam and begins diverting a stream toward the tents.
The Fallen Canopy
You lure the swarm away with one sack and save the remaining supplies.
Sacrifice one sack
The lids slam shut just before the swarm reaches the dry stores.
Seal every crate
Smoke drives the swarm off long enough to seal the stores.
Smoke the sacks
A cloud of fist-sized insects drops onto open food sacks. Cooks swat the air with lids while the first creatures are already tearing through the canvas.
The Hungry Cloud
You save the rest without risking the bank any further.
Abandon two barrels
The ground gives way under your feet and steam burns you before you can retreat.
You find a seam of cold rock that lets you recover the entire stock without nearing the steam.
You move one barrel, but two others remain cut off behind scalding water.
You roll the barrels over firm ground before the water rises.
Map the cold ground
The logs form a rough bridge and the barrels come back one by one.
Lay fallen logs
A pool that was warm moments ago starts boiling around the camp's water barrels. The ground steams, ropes soften, and nobody knows which part of the bank will collapse next.
The Boiling Pool
A new line secures the equipment and lets the surveyors return.
Anchor a new line
You mark the crossing as unsafe and give up on the hanging equipment.
Close the crossing
The surveyors abandon their instruments but leave the ravine alive.
Recover only the people
Two surveyors laid fossilized bones across a ravine to reach a measuring marker. One support cracks, leaving their equipment suspended in the middle above a torrent.
Bones over the Ravine
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_long: One skiff breaks free and the other two stop pulling against each other.
Cut one anchor line
The crew Helmsman gives all three pilots one order and untangles the circle.
Let the Helmsman call it
The pilots keep the hulls apart until the current weakens.
Wait for the turn
Three skiffs anchored in a cove begin turning together when the current shifts. Their lines cross underwater, and every pilot pulls a different way to avoid the neighboring hulls.
The Circular Current
You cheer for a local who knows every bump in the flats.
Back a local racer
You help move the finish line out of the first area the tide will cover.
Hold the finish line
You miss a step, hit the ground hard, and finish the race in a puddle under the cheers.
You finish far enough ahead that the locals offer you the starting ribbon as a trophy.
You keep pace, but the wind makes you miss the final pole.
You use the stilts' flex and clear the last stretch without breaking stride.
Race the stilts
Locals set up a stilt race across a strip of land that will vanish at high tide. A gust bends the long poles, yet the competitors refuse to shorten the course.
The Stilt Race
The crew Navigator chooses the channel that will hold enough water longest.
Follow the Navigator
You read the wrong ripple and the tide surrounds the ferry before you reach the dry strip.
You find a deeper pass that lets the loaded ferry leave before the tide returns.
You free the ferry, but it must abandon part of its load on the sand.
You follow the receding current and pull the ferry into a channel that stays open long enough.
Read the returning tide
The ferry becomes light enough to push toward a shallow channel.
Unload the baskets
Low tide has stranded a small ferry loaded with baskets in the middle of wet flats. Water is returning through several channels, and the boatmen no longer know which one will reach the sea first.
Ferry on the Flats
The tents collapse and the animal simply steps over the slack lines.
Drop the tents
The herd changes direction and gives the camp room to recover.
Throw food away
You pull at the wrong moment and a long leg sends you rolling through the grass.
You turn the lines into a wide loop and calmly guide the whole herd around the tents.
You free one rope, but the animal leaves with two stakes still attached.
You release tension one rope at a time and the animal gets out without tearing down camp.
Untangle line by line
A long-legged animal walks through camp and tangles itself in four tent lines. Every movement tears out another stake while the rest of the herd approaches, sniffing curiously.
Legs in the Lines
Several adults shove each cart through the mud to firm ground together.
Form a push line
The camp sacrifices gear and gets the carts moving before the route closes.
Leave the heavy poles
The children reach high ground while the adults finish loading.
Move the children first
A nomad camp delays packing until the tide begins closing the paths across the flats. The carts are still half loaded, and children gather animals that refuse to move.
Camp in the Tide
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_rout: The stitching shows which half was moved after the pennant was placed.
Compare the fabric
You only note the place and continue without trusting the marker.
Ignore the symbol
You stop the misleading pennant from turning further and leave a warning.
Tie both halves down
Two months later, a pennant bearing the same symbol hangs from a current marker. It has been cut in half, and each half now points toward a different channel.
The Split Pennant
The scratches retain enough pigment to reconstruct the old direction.
Copy the old outline
At least the marker stops giving a false bearing.
Leave the board bare
You replace the arrow with a symbol that simply tells crews to verify the current.
Paint a neutral warning
Farther along the route, a painted arrow has been scraped back to bare wood. A local pilot says several similar markers changed just before foreign crews passed through.
The Scraped Arrow
You carve an observation rule instead of a fixed direction.
Carve a current rule
You remove the marker so no crew mistakes it for reliable guidance again.
Remove the board
You pass on what you found and leave the local pilots to decide on a new system.
Leave it to the locals
A final marker carries the symbol intact but no arrow. At its base, several crews carved their own corrections; the sabotage has finally made the marker network useless to everyone.
The Last Board
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_saba: The membrane bursts beneath you and you fall with two baskets into the market.
You also secure the hanging crate before it can fall onto the crowd.
You slow the lift, but one crate comes loose and smashes an empty stall.
You catch the safety line and guide the lift toward a clear trunk.
Catch the safety line
Vendors pull customers out of the area before the membrane bursts.
Clear the market
The baskets descend on ropes and lighten the lift before it fails.
Lower the baskets
A bubble lift loaded with baskets rises between two mangroves when its membrane turns white. A crowd passes underneath, and the operator frantically searches his tools for the safety line.
The Bursting Lift
The crate falls into the cleared area and nobody is hit.
Cut it over clear ground
Several hands pull together and bring the crate back onto the platform.
Haul it back
A second rope takes the weight and the crate reaches the ground gently.
Lower it by rope
The lift is almost stable, but one crate hangs by a single strap above the cleared market. The operator can cut it loose or try to haul it back onto the platform.
The Hanging Crate
Workers clear the area so the line can be bled with nobody beneath it.
Clear the walkway
You tighten the wrong valve and a pocket of hot resin splashes your arm.
You isolate the line without shutting down the other vats and avoid stopping the whole yard.
You reduce the leak, but the work area must be evacuated to clean the sticky floor.
You find the cracked joint and cut pressure just upstream.
Isolate the line
The crew Shipwright spots the bypass valve and isolates the line cleanly.
Let the Shipwright handle it
In a coating yard, a resin pipe leaks above a walkway. The floor turns slick, two workers are trapped beyond the valve, and the vat keeps pushing hot mixture through the line.
Resin Under Pressure
A harbor clerk publicly confirms the seller has no authorization.
Fetch a real clerk
You leave before the broker invents another story.
Leave the newcomers
The buyers compare their papers and put their money away.
Point out the bad stamp
A man sells supposedly official berthing papers beneath a tree, but his stamp carries the wrong grove number. Two newly arrived crews are already preparing to pay him an advance.
The Broker Without an Office
A few porters move barriers and create a pedestrian lane around the toll.
Open the side lane
The group hesitates before a line that collectively refuses to move or pay.
Stand with the merchants
The merchants turn back before the jam traps them between both groups.
Turn the carts around
An armed group blocks a narrow passage beneath a root and demands payment from every cart. Merchants pile up behind them while a second route begins filling too.
Passage Under the Root
The crew First Mate organizes the movement and keeps the boats from blocking each other.
Follow the First Mate
You follow the wrong channel and emerge directly into a patrol line you must avoid in a hurry.
You combine root contours and patrol timing to reach the exit without ever crossing their route.
You find a way out, but it costs enough time to miss your passage window.
You read the bubble drift and choose a channel that stays clear between two patrols.
Pick the quiet channel
The boatmen let the patrol pass and then take the main channel.
Wait for the patrol
Among the mangrove roots, several channels meet near a watched sector. Boatmen wait for a patrol to pass, but surface bubbles show a secondary current has just shifted.
Channels Among Roots
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_thri: Someone watches the gate while the rest of the group looks for the chain’s owner.
Post a guard
You force the chain and the gate rebounds into you when something pulls from the other side.
You open it just enough to get the trapped travelers out without letting the gate bang in the fog.
The chain gives, but the noise draws movement all around the cemetery.
You find the secondary latch hidden under moss and open the gate without ringing the bars.
Open it quietly
The travelers explain where they entered and wait while you look for another exit.
Talk through the bars
A cemetery gate is chained from the outside while two travelers call from the other side. Shapes move between the stones, and nobody recognizes the chain wrapped around the gate.
The Cemetery Gate
The salvagers leave through the side before the plaster comes down.
Clear the side door
They abandon the haul and gain enough time to clear the entrance.
Drop the chandeliers
You block the entrances after everyone leaves so another salvager does not enter.
Mark the room unsafe
In an abandoned dining hall, salvagers pull down chandeliers when a cable groans overhead. A long crack runs across the ceiling, and the main door is blocked by furniture.
Ceiling for Dinner
You tie scraps of cloth to stones along the real path.
Mark the real path
The remaining travelers return to the paving as soon as the false path disappears.
Snuff the false lamps
You follow a flame that is too steady and step into a pit hidden under leaves.
You find the dark cord linking several false lanterns and reveal where they are being controlled.
You prove one lantern is false, but two travelers have already vanished behind the trees.
You compare the heights and spot hand-placed lamps away from the true path.
Test the lantern line
In the fog, a row of lanterns leads travelers away from the paved path. The flames barely move despite the wind, and recent footprints stop abruptly near the trees.
Lying Lanterns
The chest reaches an open yard before anyone touches the lock.
Drag it outside
The salvagers mark the shed and decide the contents are not worth the risk.
Leave it shut
The knocks follow an irregular rhythm that sounds more like an animal than a person.
Listen before opening
An iron-banded chest pounds from the inside at the back of a shed. Two salvagers want to open it immediately, while a third points to fresh claw marks around the lock.
The Pounding Chest
You strike the wrong fitting; the chain lashes your shoulder before vanishing into the fog.
You reset the chain quietly and spot a mark showing it was moved recently.
You slow the slide, but the anchor catches something below the surface and stays jammed.
You follow the chain's tension and secure the link jumping out of its guide.
Catch the bad link
Bystanders leave the impact area while the barge drifts slowly.
Clear the pilings
An iron bar locks the mechanism until the chain can be hauled back.
Wedge the ratchet
A heavy mooring chain slides on its own along a fogbound quay. The ratchet no longer holds, and every lost meter brings a dark barge closer to a row of pilings.
Chain in the Fog
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_wate: The food moves first; mechanics wait for the next slot.
Prioritize the food
The repair parts move first; food sellers protest but keep the next slot.
Prioritize the parts
The crews load from half the pier each and accept a slower pace for everyone.
Split the pier
Two dock crews claim the same pier for urgent cargo. One carries food, the other repair parts, and the harbormaster refuses to choose in front of his own workers.
Pier Number Four
The gondoliers open a lane and the punt eventually reaches an empty quay.
Clear the junction
You jump onto the wrong side and the punt throws you against the quay at the first turn.
You ride a canal wave and bring the punt alongside an empty quay without touching anything.
You slow the punt, but it clips a gondola loaded with crates.
You reach the tiller before the junction and avoid the line of gondolas.
Jump for the tiller
A gondola catches the line and slows the punt before the junction.
Throw a line
A delivery punt slides riderless down a canal after its rope snaps. Ahead, a junction is crowded with gondolas, and the vendor chasing it cannot swim.
The Runaway Punt
The punt rides up a side ramp before reaching the gate.
Beach the punt
You pull the emergency chain and slow the gate enough to pass.
Grab the chain
The operator stops the gate inches above the gunwale.
Shout to the operator
The punt clears the junction, then a canal gate begins dropping ahead. The mechanism is already halfway down, and the operator has not seen the boat coming.
The Canal Gate
The workers clear the bay before any more fasteners shift.
Clear the bay
The crew Shipwright recognizes the brace twist and has the joint reset.
Let the Shipwright read it
You load the brace too quickly; a rivet pops and a plank drops onto the lower deck.
You also spot a batch of defective rivets before they are installed elsewhere.
You steady the scaffold, but the yard must close the bay to replace several fasteners.
You identify the joint taking the load sideways and have it reset correctly.
Trace the bad joint
In a shipyard, scaffolding groans above an open hull. A foreman notices three rivet heads vibrating together while workers keep carrying planks underneath.
Singing Rivets
The block closes immediately without waiting for the argument to be settled.
Follow harbor orders
Goods move to higher shelves while the shutters close.
Move the low crates
You call the wrong hour and several merchants leave their stalls exposed to the first surge.
You find an old forgotten mark that gives the whole block a few extra minutes.
You understand the danger, but too late to save every crate stacked at canal level.
You cross-check the height marks and get shutters closed before the sudden rise.
Read the water marks
A tide siren sounds earlier than expected and merchants argue over the actual surge time. Wet marks on the walls already show the canal is rising.
Marks on the Wall
Buyer and seller pull the same rope and postpone their dispute until after the rescue.
Make both sides pull
The lumber is caught before the bridge and the sale can resume.
Secure the lumber
Boatmen close the passage beneath the bridge before the raft reaches it.
Warn the bridge
A rafted lot of lumber breaks loose during a sale and drifts toward a low bridge. Buyer and seller are still arguing over who is responsible for it.
The Floating Lot
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_whis: Half the brawlers stay inside; the street regains enough room to move.
Bar the tavern door
The drivers shove with you and save their cargo from the melee.
Pull the carts clear
Your intervention puts you between two thrown stools; you take the hit and the room erupts.
You turn the two ringleaders against each other verbally, and the crowd laughs instead of swinging.
You separate one pair, but the fight spills toward loaded carts outside the door.
Your voice creates a pause long enough to pull the carts clear.
Shout them down
A tavern brawl spills toward three carts loaded with bottles. The drivers are pinned against a wall while fighters already tear off sideboards to use as clubs.
The Cart Brawl
The courier opens it just enough to show contracts stamped by several ports.
Demand the seal
You slide it under flour sacks until the hunters move on.
Hide the satchel
The courier takes the satchel back and vanishes into a rear yard.
Refuse the package
A breathless courier pushes a sealed satchel toward you and points at three hunters searching the inns. He swears it holds only shipping contracts but refuses to show the inner seal.
The Courier’s Satchel
The crowd points out the drawing’s mistakes and the copyist loses his leverage.
Mock the likeness
You destroy the copy he is waving, but he claims to have more.
Tear up one copy
Denied a scene, the copyist looks for an easier target.
Walk past
A street copyist waves a portrait that vaguely resembles you and promises to sell it to bounty hunters. He demands money to destroy the other copies in front of an amused crowd.
Portrait for Sale
You step onto a rotten tile that gives way; the thief gains two rooftops.
You force the thief down exactly in front of the owner of the stolen chit.
You follow the trail, but the thief throws the mooring chit into an unreachable gutter.
You cut across a balcony and block the next ledge.
Chase over the roofs
You cover his only safe way down and the thief eventually drops the chit.
Cut toward the gutter
The harbor suspends the ship move while the chase continues.
Warn the harbormaster
